note: Analyst self-report and an independent reviewer's findings; the reviewer saw only the sources and the accepted handoffs. Findings are claims to verify; GFL's revolver finding was checked against the 6-K notes.

analyst.notes:
The report was published (exit 0), and the run's own message says "Automated checks only: review the handoffs against the sources before use." All five modules were accepted on the first attempt with no feedback. The check is structural: headings, hashes, issuer name, as-of date and selector tables.

Defects I know are in the accepted handoffs. They cannot be replaced, and I did not edit them.
- CP-1: the "Latest quarter changes" section has a garbled net debt bullet ("fell to 28,079 from 27,438... see note"). The sources show net debt rose from 27,438 (Q1 deck) to 28,079 (Q3 deck). The same section's "conservative" wording about the leverage ratio is confusing; the ratio actually overstates leverage relative to management's adjusted EBITDAR.
- CP-1A: it says revenue was a record in each of the last three quarters. Only the Q1 and Q2 decks say that; the Q3 deck does not. The PSP-notes locator in its timeline is imprecise. I added a correction note for the CP-1 bullet inside CP-1A.
- CP-2: it implies partner cash is the collateral base of the AAdvantage Financing. The filing lists loyalty program assets among collateral and does not say that.
- CP-5: one T5.1 cell for CP-1A has a sloppy hash fragment, though the full hash is given. CP-5 lists all of the above as open issues.

Analytical limits carried in the report. Leverage and coverage use AAG consolidated inputs and EBITDA built from income-statement lines, not American's own figures or management's adjusted EBITDAR. No executed credit agreements or indentures are in the pack, so covenant thresholds, guarantors and recovery are not assessed. Discrete Q3 cash flow is derived by difference across filings, and the decks were read as text only.

Instruction and tool issues.
- "page:N" in the sources is a 3,000-character text chunk, not a printed page. The sources' inner "sha256" header (the original HTML hash) differs from the pinned jsonl hashes, which the handoffs must use.
- The method files are long and mix JSON-era rules with Markdown transport. CP-5 asks for 17 registers, and the template's disqualifier strings (for example "source-limited") must be avoided in the text.
- One shared helper script in the scratchpad was overwritten by another process mid-run, so I used a separate script.
- The system date changed to 2026-11-06 during the run. I kept the as-of date at 2026-11-05 as instructed.

mismatches.claim: Counter-evidence: record revenue in each of the last three quarters per the decks
mismatches.source_value: Q1 deck says record first-quarter revenue ($13.9bn) and Q2 deck says record quarterly revenue ($16.7bn), but Q3 revenue of 16,335 is below Q2 at 16,735 and the Q3 deck (EX-99.2 2026-10-22) makes no record claim. Not corrected in the delivered text; only flagged in CP-5 T5.2.

mismatches.module: CP-1 (Latest quarter changes bullet, net debt)
mismatches.claim: Net debt on the management definition fell to 28,079 from 27,438
mismatches.source_value: Net debt rose: 27,438 at 31 Mar 2026 to 28,079 at 30 Sep 2026 (total debt 34,732 to 36,366). The bullet contradicts itself ('see note') and leaves the wrong direction in the accepted answer. CP-1A and CP-2 correct it, but CP-1 as delivered is unchanged.

mismatches.claim: LTM EBITDAR from income-statement lines is 'conservative in the sense of being lower on EBITDAR'
mismatches.source_value: A lower EBITDAR gives higher leverage, so the 6.80x/8.81x ratios overstate leverage against management's definition. Management's Q1 adjusted EBITDAR includes D&A of 566 and rent of 311, with regional amounts in regional expenses. The wording is contradictory; CP-1A and CP-5 correct the direction.
mismatches.source_location: EX-99.2 2026-04-23 page:11 (EBITDAR build); 10-K page:143 (cash-flow D&A 2,219 vs income-statement 1,890)

mismatches.claim: Partner cash is also the collateral base of the AAdvantage Financing
mismatches.source_value: The 10-Q lists loyalty program assets among collateral and does not say partner cash is the collateral base. This overstates recovery support. CP-5 flags it but the delivered CP-2 text is unchanged.
mismatches.source_location: 10-Q Q3 page:16 (collateral list); 10-K page:13 (6.2bn partner cash)

mismatches.claim: Cash plus undrawn facilities of 4,634 against the 2,000 minimum liquidity covenant
mismatches.source_value: The covenant is at least $2.0bn of unrestricted cash and cash equivalents plus amounts available under revolving credit facilities. Excluding short-term investments (7,163) is labelled indicative. Undrawn facilities of 3,510 include a 50 cargo facility expiring December 2026, so the figure is not a covenant calculation.

omissions.topic: No American-perimeter leverage or coverage, although American is the issuer
omissions.why_material: All EBITDA, interest and leverage ratios (C4, C6, C13 to C15) use AAG inputs. These include the unsecured PSP notes (3,746) and AAG-only items. American's own statements are in the same 10-Q and could be used: debt and finance leases 25,876 vs 29,635 at AAG, operating income 535 vs 521, interest expense net 1,231 vs 1,242 for nine months, D&A 1,442. The issuer's own leverage and coverage are therefore not computed. CP-5 flags this as GAP-003 but it was not fixed.
omissions.source_location: 10-Q Q3 page:25 to page:27; CP-1 C13 to C15

omissions.topic: Covenant thresholds and headroom (LTV, minimum 2.0bn liquidity, AAdvantage peak DSCR)
omissions.why_material: The filing states compliance but gives no thresholds, test dates or headroom. The modules acknowledge this and mark it Not calculable. A credit reader still has no tested view of the secured, collateral-coverage-driven structure, which is the main refinancing route. Executed documents are not in the pack.

omissions.topic: Guarantee and security structure by instrument
omissions.why_material: The modules say guarantor identity is not supplied. The 10-Q shows AAG as co-party to the 2013, 2014 and 2023 credit agreements, and AAdvantage Loyalty IP Ltd. (Cayman) as co-issuer of the AAdvantage Financing. The ranking of the 2026-1 Class (B)R junior equipment notes (870) behind existing equipment notes is also not carried into the structure analysis. This affects the structural subordination and recovery read.

omissions.topic: Non-debt contractual claims and sensitivities not quantified
omissions.why_material: Regional capacity purchase agreements (4,461), other purchase obligations (19,612) and retiree medical (1,072) sit inside the 90,315 total. CP-1 gives only the total, the debt rows, leases and aircraft commitments. Also omitted: the 10-Q fuel price and floating-rate interest sensitivities (page:45, page:68), NOLs of about 11.9bn and other carryforwards of 6.0bn (page:20), and the pension funding position beyond the 1,099 liability. These are fixed claims ahead of debt service and weigh on the 2028 refinancing view.

omissions.topic: Published CP-1/CP-1A/CP-2 text keeps defects that CP-5 identified
omissions.why_material: CP-5 lists three or four material defects (net debt direction, the unsupported record-revenue claim, the partner-cash collateral claim, AAG vs American perimeter). The accepted modules were not edited, so a reader of CP-1, CP-1A or CP-2 alone is misled. CP-5 itself notes 'Reader of CP-1 alone is misled'.
omissions.source_location: deliveries/3a5252fc.../CP-1.md, CP-1A.md, CP-2.md; CP-5 T5.2 and T5.6

cutoff_issues: No cutoff breach. The latest source is the Q3 10-Q signed 2026-10-22 and the Q3 deck of 2026-10-22, both before 2026-11-05. October 2026 events (A320 option exercise, NEA class-certification opposition) are labelled as subsequent events.

The Q4 and full-year 2026 outlook is labelled as a management forecast dated 2026-10-22. LTM, 'Q3 2026 discrete' and nine-month labels are used correctly. The 'Q3 discrete' cash flow is derived by difference and labelled derived.
review.summary: I checked 62 load-bearing figures against the pinned filings and decks, and all 62 matched the cited page and value. The set covered revenue, operating income, net income, cash, short-term investments and the debt lines. It also covered the Note 5 components, undrawn facilities and liquidity, the American maturity ladder, interest expense, cash flow, and the management total and net debt. I recomputed every derived item and all reproduce: C1 to C18 including LTM EBITDA 2,891, EBITDAR 4,127, interest 1,664, the 1.74x, 0.58x and 1.42x coverage ratios, 10.25x, 8.81x, 6.80x and 6.70x leverage, and FCF 1,813 and (91). There are no cutoff breaches. The defects are in the narrative, not the numbers. First, CP-1A's claim of record revenue in each of the last three quarters is wrong, because Q3 revenue of 16,335 is below Q2 at 16,735. Second, the CP-1 net debt bullet says 'fell' when net debt rose, and the EBITDAR 'conservative' wording points the wrong way. Third, CP-2 treats partner cash as AAdvantage collateral, which the filing does not say. All three were identified by CP-5 and corrected downstream, but the accepted answers and deliverable were left unedited. The main substantive gap is that the issuer is American, yet all leverage and coverage is on the AAG perimeter, with no American-level ratios although the data is in the 10-Q. Covenant thresholds, headroom and guarantor detail are unavailable without executed documents, and the modules say so openly. The report is fit for liquidity, earnings and maturity views once these corrections are carried. It is not fit for covenant, recovery or issuer-level leverage use."
